requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.condition: inpar is a template that can match values of different sizes
requirements.canonical: Calling `sizeof` with a template that can match values of different sizes SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: when inpar is a template and it can match values of different sizes;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.condition: inpar is not of a record or set type
requirements.canonical: Calling `sizeof` with an argument that is not of a record or set type SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: the template passed to the inpar parameter is not of a record or set type.

ambiguity.issue: The error case names only 'the template', although sizeof also accepts values; the rule is read as applying to any argument.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.canonical: The `istemplatekind` predefined function has the signature istemplatekind(in template any_type invalue, in charstring kind) return boolean.
requirements.original: istemplatekind (in template any_type invalue, in charstring kind) return boolean

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.canonical: The `istemplatekind` function IS a function to examine whether a template contains a certain kind of matching mechanism.
requirements.original: This function allows to examine if a template contains a certain kind of the matching mechanisms.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.condition: kind denotes specific value, a matching mechanism instead of values or a matching character pattern
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is specific value (B.1.1), a matching mechanism instead of values (B.1.2) or matching character pattern (B.1.5), `istemplatekind` SHALL return true if the content of `invalue` is of the same kind.
requirements.original: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is matching a specific value (clause B.1.1), a matching mechanism instead of values (clause B.1.2) or matching character pattern (clause B.1.5), the function shall return true if the content of the invalue parameter is of the same kind.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.condition: kind denotes a matching mechanism inside values
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching mechanism inside values (B.1.3), `istemplatekind` SHALL return true if the template in `invalue` contains this kind of matching mechanism on the first level of nesting.
requirements.original: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching mechanism inside values (clause B.1.3), the function shall return true if the template in the invalue parameter contains this kind of matching mechanism on the first level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.condition: kind denotes a matching attribute
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching attribute (B.1.4), `istemplatekind` SHALL return true only if the template in `invalue` has this kind of matching attribute attached to it directly, not to a field of `invalue` at any level of nesting.
requirements.original: If the matching mechanism kind enquired is a matching attribute (clause B.1.4), the function shall return true if the template in the invalue parameter has this kind of matching attribute attached to it directly (i.e. it doesn't count if the attribute is attached to a field of invalue at any level of nesting).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.canonical: In all cases not covered by the rules for specific values, matching mechanisms instead of values, patterns, matching mechanisms inside values and matching attributes, `istemplatekind` SHALL return false.
requirements.original: In all other cases the function returns false.

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter of `istemplatekind` SHALL be one of the strings listed in table C.1.
requirements.original: The kind parameter shall be one of the strings listed in table C.1.

requirements.subject: ent:templatekind-type
requirements.canonical: Clause E.2.2.5 defines the type `TemplateKind` and a constant for each allowed value of the `kind` parameter of `istemplatekind`.
requirements.original: NOTE: Clause E.2.2.5 includes the type definition TemplateKind and a constant for each of the allowed values of the kind parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.canonical: The `istemplatekind` function SHOULD be used in combination with the `TemplateKind` type and its constants defined in clause E.2.2.5.
requirements.original: It is recommended to use the istemplatekind function in combination with this type and these constants to ease the checking of correct usage and to improve the readability of test specs.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 apply to the `istemplatekind` function in addition to its specific restrictions.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes given in clause 16.1.2, the following restrictions apply:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-istemplatekind
requirements.condition: kind is not one of the values of table C.1
requirements.canonical: Calling `istemplatekind` with a `kind` argument that is not one of the values stated in table C.1 SHALL lead to an error.
requirements.original: a) Calling the istemplatekind function with a different second parameter than stated in table C.1 shall lead to an error.

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "value" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the specific value matching mechanism (clause B.1.1).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "value"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Specific value; Col3: B.1.1

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "list" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the template list matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.1).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "list"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Template list; Col3: B.1.2.1

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "complement" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the complemented template list matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.2).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "complement"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Complemented template list; Col3: B.1.2.2

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "AnyValue" or "?" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the any value matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.3).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "AnyValue", "?"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Any value; Col3: B.1.2.3

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "AnyValueOrNone" or "*" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the any value or none matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.4).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "AnyValueOrNone", "*"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Any value or none; Col3: B.1.2.4

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "range" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the value range matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.5).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "range"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Value range; Col3: type map from charstring to charstring MyMap; template MyMap mw_myMessageTemplate4 := { ["host"] := "::1", ["port"] := * }; v_mybooleanVar := match ({ ["host"] := "::1", ["port"] := 80 }, mw_myMessageTemplate4); // matches and returns true v_mybooleanVar := match ({ ["host"] := "::1" }, mw_myMessageTemplate4); // matches and returns true B.1.2.5

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "superset" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the SuperSet matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.6).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "superset"; Allowed values of kind parameter: SuperSet; Col3: B.1.2.6

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "subset" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the SubSet matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.7).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "subset"; Allowed values of kind parameter: SubSet; Col3: B.1.2.7

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "omit" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the omit matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.8).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "omit"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Omit; Col3: B.1.2.8

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "decmatch" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the matching decoded content matching mechanism (clause B.1.2.9).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "decmatch"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Matching decoded content; Col3: B.1.2.9

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "AnyElement" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the any element matching mechanism (clause B.1.3.1).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "AnyElement"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Any element; Col3: B.1.3.1

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "AnyElementsOrNone" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the any number of elements or none matching mechanism (clause B.1.3.2).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "AnyElementsOrNone"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Any number of elements or none; Col3: B.1.3.2

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "permutation" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the permutation matching mechanism (clause B.1.3.3).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "permutation"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Permutation; Col3: B.1.3.3

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "length" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the length restriction matching mechanism (clause B.1.4.1).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "length"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Length restriction; Col3: B.1.4.1

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "ifpresent" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the the ifpresent indicator matching mechanism (clause B.1.4.2).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "ifpresent"; Allowed values of kind parameter: The IfPresent indicator; Col3: B.1.4.2

requirements.subject: ent:kind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `kind` parameter value "pattern" of `istemplatekind` IS the selector for the matching character pattern matching mechanism (clause B.1.5).
requirements.original: Table C.1:: "pattern"; Allowed values of kind parameter: Matching character pattern; Col3: B.1.5

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The `regexp` predefined function has the syntax regexp [@nocase] (in template (value) any inpar, in template (present) any expression, in integer groupno) return any_character_string_type.
requirements.original:
regexp [@nocase] (
    in template (value) any inpar,
    in template (present) any expression,
    in integer groupno
  ) return any_character_string_type

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The `regexp` function SHALL first match the inpar actual parameter (or, if inpar is a template, its value equivalent) against the expression actual parameter according to the pattern matching rules of clause B.1.5.
requirements.original: This function first matches the parameter inpar (or in case inpar is a template, its value equivalent) against the expression in the second parameter according to the pattern matching specified in clause B.1.5.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: expression is not a template containing a pattern matching mechanism
requirements.canonical: If the expression actual parameter of `regexp` is not a template containing a pattern matching mechanism, the `regexp` function SHALL process it as if it was a character pattern as described in clause B.1.5.
requirements.original: If expression is not a template containing a pattern matching mechanism, it shall be processed by this predefined function as if it was a character pattern as described in clause B.1.5.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: the @nocase modifier is present
requirements.canonical: If the `@nocase` modifier is present in a `regexp` call, the matching of that call SHALL be done in a case-insensitive way as specified in clause B.1.5.6.
requirements.original: If the @nocase modifier is present, this and all subsequent matchings shall be done in a case-insensitive way, as specified in clause B.1.5.6.

readings: If the `@nocase` modifier is present in a `regexp` call, the matching of that call SHALL be done in a case-insensitive way.
If the `@nocase` modifier is present in a `regexp` call, that matching and all matchings performed subsequently (e.g. in later statements or calls) SHALL be done in a case-insensitive way.
ambiguity.issue: "this and all subsequent matchings" has no defined referent for "subsequent"; the reading limited to the matching(s) of the same call is chosen because the modifier is part of the call syntax.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: inpar is a literal without explicitly given type
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is a literal whose type is not explicitly given, the type of inpar SHALL be retrieved from the value contents.
requirements.original: If inpar is a literal (i.e. type is not explicitly given) the corresponding type shall be retrieved from the value contents.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: the matching is unsuccessful
requirements.canonical: If the matching of inpar against expression is unsuccessful, the `regexp` function SHALL return an empty string.
requirements.original: If this matching is unsuccessful, an empty string shall be returned.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: the matching is successful
requirements.canonical: If the matching of inpar against expression is successful, the `regexp` function SHALL return the substring of inpar that matched the group of expression with group number groupno.
requirements.original: If this matching is successful, the substring of inpar shall be returned, which matched the groupno-s group of expression during the matching.

requirements.subject: ent:group-number
requirements.canonical: The group numbers of an expression of `regexp` ARE assigned in the order of occurrence of the opening bracket of each group, counting from 0 in steps of 1.
requirements.original: Group numbers are assigned by the order of occurrences of the opening bracket of a group and counted starting from 0 by step 1.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The inpar and expression actual parameters of `regexp` SHALL each be a value or a template of `charstring` or `universal charstring` type.
requirements.original: The parameters inpar and expression shall be a value or a template of charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: inpar is a template
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value matching mechanism only.
requirements.original: In case inpar is a template, it shall contain the specific value matching mechanism only.

readings: If inpar of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value matching mechanism only.
If inpar of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value or character pattern matching mechanism only.
ambiguity.issue: This sentence allows only specific value, while the error cause in C.4.1-s018 only lists matching mechanisms other than specific value or character pattern; the text of this sentence (together with the formal parameter restriction template (value)) is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: expression is a template
requirements.canonical: If the expression actual parameter of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain only the specific value or pattern matching mechanisms.
requirements.original: When expression is a template it shall contain the specific value or pattern matching mechanisms only.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The groupno actual parameter of `regexp` SHALL be a non-negative integer.
requirements.original: The parameter groupno shall be a non-negative integer.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The type of the character string returned by `regexp` IS the root type of the inpar actual parameter.
requirements.original: The type of the character string returned is the root type of inpar.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: Unlike other well-known regular expression implementations, the `regexp` function matches the whole inpar string instead of only a substring.
requirements.original: NOTE: This function differs from other well-known regular expression matching implementations in that: a) It matches the whole inpar string instead of only a substring.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: Unlike some other regular expression implementations, the `regexp` function starts counting groups from 0, and group 0 IS the first group rather than the whole matched substring.
requirements.original: b) It starts counting groups from 0, while in some other implementations the first group is referenced by 1 and the whole substring matched by the expression is referenced by 0.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `regexp` in addition to the error causes specific to `regexp`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: inpar is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is a template that contains a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: when inpar is a template, it contains other matching mechanism than specific value or character pattern;

readings: An error SHALL occur if inpar is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern.
An error SHALL occur if inpar is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value (as required by C.4.1-s010).
ambiguity.issue: Conflicts with C.4.1-s010, which allows only the specific value matching mechanism for inpar; the literal text of this error cause is used.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: expression is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern
requirements.canonical: If the expression actual parameter of `regexp` is a template that contains a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: when expression is a template, it contains other matching mechanism than specific value or character pattern;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: inpar is charstring and expression is universal charstring
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `regexp` is of `charstring` type and the expression actual parameter is of `universal charstring` type, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `inpar is of charstring type and expression is of universal charstring type;`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: groupno is negative
requirements.canonical: If the groupno actual parameter of `regexp` is a negative integer, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: groupno is a negative integer;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-regexp
requirements.condition: expression has no group with number groupno
requirements.canonical: If the expression of `regexp` contains no group with group number groupno, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: there is no groupno -s group in expression.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: The `substr` predefined function has the syntax substr(in template (present) any inpar, in integer index, in integer count) return input_string_or_sequence_type.
requirements.original:
substr(
   in template (present) any inpar, 
   in integer index, 
   in integer count
  ) return input_string_or_sequence_type

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: The `substr` function returns a substring or subsequence of a value of a binary string type (`bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`), a character string type (`charstring`, `universal charstring`) or a sequence type (`record of`, `set of` or array).
requirements.original: This function returns a substring or subsequence from a value that is of a binary string type (bitstring, hexstring, octetstring), a character string type (charstring, universal charstring), or a sequence type (record of, set of or array).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is a literal without explicitly given type
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `substr` is a literal whose type is not explicitly given, the type of inpar SHALL be retrieved from the value contents.
requirements.original: If inpar is a literal (i.e. type is not explicitly given) the corresponding type shall be retrieved from the value contents.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: The type of the substring or subsequence returned by `substr` IS the root type of the inpar actual parameter.
requirements.original: The type of the substring or subsequence returned is the root type of the input parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: The index actual parameter of `substr` defines the starting point of the substring or subsequence to return.
requirements.original: The starting point of substring or subsequence to return is defined by the second parameter (index).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: Indexing of inpar in `substr` starts from zero.
requirements.original: Indexing starts from zero.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: The count actual parameter of `substr` defines the length of the substring or subsequence to be returned.
requirements.original: The third input parameter (count) defines the length of the substring or subsequence to be returned.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: For string types, the unit of length of the count parameter of `substr` IS as defined in table 4.
requirements.original: The units of length for string types are as defined in table 4 of the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: For sequence types, the unit of length of the count parameter of `substr` IS element.
requirements.original: For sequence types, the unit of length is element.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is an array
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `substr` is an array, the returned type IS `record of`, because the root type of an array is `record of`.
requirements.original: NOTE: Note that the root types of arrays is record of, therefore if inpar is an array the returned type is record of.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is an array
requirements.canonical: When inpar of `substr` is an array, the indexing in inpar and in the returned `record of` value CAN differ.
requirements.original: This, in some cases, may lead to different indexing in inpar and in the returned value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is a template of a character or binary string type
requirements.canonical: When `substr` is used on a template of a character or binary string type, inpar MAY contain any template that fulfils the requirements for referencing individual string elements on the right hand side of an assignment specified in clause 15.6.1.
requirements.original: When used on templates of character and binary string types, inpar can contain any template that fulfils the requirements for referencing individual string elements on the right hand side of an assignment specified in clause 15.6.1.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is a template of a character or binary string type
requirements.canonical: When `substr` is used on a string template, the index and count parameters SHALL be interpreted according to the rules for indexing of string templates of clause 15.6.1, i.e. count counts indexable items.
requirements.original: The rules for the indexing of string templates specified in the same section are used for interpreting the index and count parameters, i.e. the count parameter counts indexable items.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is a string template
requirements.canonical: When used on a template of a character or binary string type, `substr` returns a template determined by the rules of clause C.4.2.
requirements.original: The substr function then returns a template according to the following rules:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains a specific value
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template of `substr` contains a specific value, `substr` SHALL return a specific value.
requirements.original: A specific value is returned if the referenced template contains a specific value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains a pattern
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template of `substr` contains a pattern, `substr` SHALL return a pattern.
requirements.original: A pattern is returned if the referenced template contains a pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: template of binary string type containing AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template of `substr` is of a binary string type and contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone, `substr` SHALL return a specific value containing as many AnyElement symbols as the count parameter.
requirements.original: A specific value containing as many AnyElement symbols as is the count parameter is returned if the referenced template if of a binary string type and contains the AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol.

ambiguity.issue: Typo "template if of a binary string type" should read "template is of a binary string type".

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: binary string template containing AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: If the referenced binary string template of `substr` contains AnyValueOrNone, the `ifpresent` matching attribute SHALL be added to the returned value.
requirements.original: In case of the AnyValueOrNone matching symbol, the ifpresent matching attribute shall be added to the returned value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: template of character string type containing AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template of `substr` is of a character string type and contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone, `substr` SHALL return a pattern containing as many ? metacharacters as the count parameter.
requirements.original: A pattern containing as many ? metacharacters as is the count parameter is returned if the referenced template if of a character string type and contains the AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol.

ambiguity.issue: Typo "template if of a character string type" should read "template is of a character string type".

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: character string template containing AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: If the referenced character string template of `substr` contains AnyValueOrNone, the `ifpresent` matching attribute SHALL be added to the returned pattern.
requirements.original: In case of the AnyValueOrNone matching symbol, the ifpresent matching attribute shall be added to the returned value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar contains a length matching attribute
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `substr` contains a length matching attribute, the value returned by `substr` SHALL NOT contain that length matching attribute.
requirements.original: If inpar contains a length matching attribute, the returned value shall be without this attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar contains the ifpresent matching attribute
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `substr` contains the `ifpresent` matching attribute, the value returned by `substr` SHALL also contain the `ifpresent` matching attribute.
requirements.original: If inpar contains the ifpresent matching attribute, the returned value shall contain this attribute as well.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar refers to a present-restricted template or to a mandatory/unrestricted field
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `substr` contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction, or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the value returned by `substr` SHALL have the present restriction.
requirements.original: If inpar contains a reference to a template with the present restriction a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record `of, set` `of or array, the` returned value shall have the present restriction.

readings: The returned value SHALL have the present restriction if inpar contains (a) a reference to a template with the present restriction, (b) a matching symbol fulfilling the present restriction, or (c) a reference to an unrestricted template field representing a mandatory record/set field or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array.

The returned value SHALL have the present restriction only if inpar contains a reference to a template with the present restriction whose content is a matching symbol fulfilling the present restriction or a reference to such an unrestricted field.
ambiguity.issue: The sentence lacks commas and is garbled by the PDF conversion, so the scope of "a reference to" is unclear; the three-alternative reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar refers to a template with value or omit restriction
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `substr` contains a reference to a template with the value or omit restriction, the value returned by `substr` SHALL have the value restriction.
requirements.original: If inpar contains a reference to a template with the value or omit restriction, the returned value shall have the value restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is a template of a sequence type or an array
requirements.canonical: When inpar of `substr` is a template of a sequence type or an array, it SHALL contain only specific values, AnyElement or combined templates whose elements are specific values, AnyElement or combined templates.
requirements.original: When inpar is a template of sequence type or is an array, only the specific value combined templates whose elements are specific values, and AnyElement matching mechanisms or combined templates are allowed and the substring or subsequence to be returned shall not contain AnyElement or combined template.

readings: inpar SHALL contain only specific values, AnyElement, or combined templates whose elements are specific values, AnyElement or combined templates.
inpar SHALL be a specific value or a combined template whose elements are only specific values, AnyElement or combined templates (AnyElement not allowed at the top level).
ambiguity.issue: The sentence "only the specific value combined templates whose elements are specific values, and AnyElement matching mechanisms or combined templates are allowed" lacks punctuation; the first reading is chosen, consistent with the error cause C.4.2-s030.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is a template of a sequence type or an array
requirements.canonical: When inpar of `substr` is a template of a sequence type or an array, the substring or subsequence to be returned SHALL NOT contain AnyElement or a combined template.
requirements.original: When inpar is a template of sequence type or is an array, only the specific value combined templates whose elements are specific values, and AnyElement matching mechanisms or combined templates are allowed and the substring or subsequence to be returned shall not contain AnyElement or combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `substr` in addition to the error causes specific to `substr`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: index < 0
requirements.canonical: If the index actual parameter of `substr` is less than zero, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `index is less than zero;`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: count < 0
requirements.canonical: If the count actual parameter of `substr` is less than zero, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `count is less than zero;` if inpar contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + count is greater than lengthof(inpar);

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + count > lengthof(inpar)
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `substr` contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + count is greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: if inpar contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + count is greater than lengthof(inpar);

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: string template with a matching mechanism not allowed for indexing
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `substr` is a template of a character or binary string type containing a matching mechanism other than those allowed for indexing in clause 15.6.1, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `inpar is a template of a character or binary string type and contains a matching mechanism other than those` allowed for indexing as specified in clause 15.6.1;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: sequence/array template with disallowed matching mechanisms
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `substr` is a template of a sequence type or array containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or combined template, or a combined template whose elements are matching mechanisms other than specific values, AnyElement or combined templates, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `inpar is a template of a sequence type or array and it contains other matching mechanism as specific value or` combined template; or if the elements of combined template are any other matching mechanisms than specific values, and AnyElement or combined templates;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-substr
requirements.condition: inpar is not of a string, record of, set of or array type
requirements.canonical: If the template passed to inpar of `substr` is not of type `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring`, `universal charstring`, `record of`, `set of` or array, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: the template passed to the inpar parameter is not of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, or array.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The `replace` predefined function has the syntax replace(in template (present) any inpar, in integer index, in integer len, in template (present) any repl) return any_string_or_sequence type.
requirements.original:
replace(
   in template (present) any inpar, 
   in integer index,
    in integer len, 
    in template (present) any repl
  ) return any_string_or_sequence type

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The `replace` function SHALL replace the substring or subsequence of inpar starting at index index with length len by repl and return the resulting string or sequence.
requirements.original: This function replaces the substring or subsequence of value inpar at index index of length len with the string or sequence value repl and returns the resulting string or sequence.

ambiguity.issue: "value inpar" and "sequence value repl" although C.4.3-s011/s013 allow templates for both parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The `replace` function SHALL NOT modify the inpar actual parameter.
requirements.original: inpar shall not be modified.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: len is 0
requirements.canonical: If len is 0, the `replace` function SHALL insert repl into inpar at position index.
requirements.original: If len is 0 the string or sequence repl is inserted.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: index is 0
requirements.canonical: If index is 0, the `replace` function SHALL insert repl at the beginning of inpar.
requirements.original: If index is 0, repl is inserted at the beginning of inpar.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: index is lengthof(inpar)
requirements.canonical: If index equals lengthof(inpar), the `replace` function SHALL insert repl at the end of inpar.
requirements.original: If index is lengthof(inpar), repl is inserted at the end of inpar.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar is a literal without explicitly given type
requirements.canonical: If the inpar actual parameter of `replace` is a literal whose type is not explicitly given, the type of inpar SHALL be retrieved from the value contents.
requirements.original: If inpar is a literal (i.e. type is not explicitly given) the corresponding type shall be retrieved from the value contents.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The inpar and repl actual parameters of `replace` and the returned string or sequence SHALL be of the same root type.
requirements.original: inpar and repl, and the returned string or sequence shall be of the same root type.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The `replace` function MAY be applied to `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, any character string, `record of`, `set of` and array values.
requirements.original: The function replace can be applied to bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, or any character string, record `of, set` `of, or arrays.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: Indexing in strings for `replace` starts from zero.
requirements.original: Note that indexing in strings starts from zero.`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar or repl is an array
requirements.canonical: If inpar or repl or both of `replace` are an array, the returned type IS `record of`, because the root type of an array is `record of`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The root types of arrays is record of, therefore if inpar or repl or both are an array, the returned type is record of.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar or repl is an array
requirements.canonical: When inpar or repl of `replace` is an array, the indexing in inpar and/or repl and in the returned value CAN differ.
requirements.original: This, in some cases, may lead to different indexing in inpar and/or repl and in the returned value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The inpar actual parameter of `replace` MAY contain a template.
requirements.original: The inpar parameter is allowed to contain a template.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar is a template
requirements.canonical: A template passed as inpar of `replace` SHALL fulfil the requirements on the inpar parameter of the `substr` function specified in clause C.4.2.
requirements.original: This template shall fulfil the requirements on the inpar parameter of the substr function specified in clause C.4.2.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The repl actual parameter of `replace` MAY contain a template.
requirements.original: The repl parameter is allowed to contain a template that shall contain a specific value, pattern or AnyValue without any matching attributes attached to it.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: repl is a template
requirements.canonical: A template passed as repl of `replace` SHALL contain only a specific value, a pattern or AnyValue, without any matching attributes attached to it.
requirements.original: The repl parameter is allowed to contain a template that shall contain a specific value, pattern or AnyValue without any matching attributes attached to it.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar or repl contains a template
requirements.canonical: If either inpar or repl of `replace` contains a template, the `replace` function SHALL return a template with the present restriction according to the rules of clause C.4.3.
requirements.original: If either the inpar or repl parameter contain a template, the replace function returns a template with the present restriction according to the following rules:

readings: If inpar or repl contains a template, the returned template SHALL always have the present restriction.
If inpar or repl contains a template, the returned template SHALL have the present restriction unless C.4.3-s025 applies (value restriction when inpar refers to a value- or omit-restricted template).
ambiguity.issue: This sentence states the present restriction unconditionally, while C.4.3-s025 requires the value restriction in some cases; the second reading is chosen as canonical intent but the canonical text keeps the stated rule.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar and repl both contain AnyValue
requirements.canonical: If both inpar and repl of `replace` contain AnyValue, `replace` SHALL return `? length (index..infinity)`.
requirements.original: `? length (index..infinity) is returned when both inpar and repl contain AnyValue`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar contains AnyValueOrNone and repl contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `replace` contains AnyValueOrNone and repl contains AnyValue, `replace` SHALL return `* length (index..infinity)`.
requirements.original: `* length (index..infinity) is returned when inpar contains AnyValueOrNone and repl` contains AnyValue

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: repl contains AnyValue, inpar is of a binary string type, and neither of the two preceding rules applies
requirements.canonical: In all other cases, when repl of `replace` contains AnyValue and inpar is of a binary string type, the AnyValue SHALL be converted, before the function is evaluated, to a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone.
requirements.original: In all other cases when the AnyValue matching symbol occurs in the repl parameter, it is automatically converted prior to resolving the function evaluation if any of the following conditions is met: To a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type

readings: AnyValue in repl SHALL be converted to a binary string with a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type.
AnyValue in repl SHALL be converted only if some further unstated condition is met, the listed items being the conditions.
ambiguity.issue: The lead-in says "if any of the following conditions is met" but the following items are conversion targets with conditions attached; the first reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: repl contains AnyValue, inpar is of a character string type, and neither of the two preceding rules applies
requirements.canonical: In all other cases, when repl of `replace` contains AnyValue and inpar is of a character string type, the AnyValue SHALL be converted, before the function is evaluated, to pattern "*".
requirements.original: In all other cases when the AnyValue matching symbol occurs in the repl parameter, it is automatically converted prior to resolving the function evaluation if any of the following conditions is met: To pattern "*" if inpar is of a character string type

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar is of a binary string type and repl contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: The AnyValue-to-AnyElementOrNone conversion of repl in `replace` SHALL produce a binary string compatible with the type of inpar.
requirements.original: To a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar is of a character string type and repl contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: When inpar of `replace` is of a character string type, the converted repl SHALL be pattern "*".
requirements.original: To pattern "*" if inpar is of a character string type

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar or repl contains a template
requirements.canonical: When inpar or repl is a template and neither of the AnyValue rules applies, `replace` SHALL return a value equal to substr(inpar, 0, index) & repl & substr(inpar, index + len, lengthof(inpar) - index - len).
requirements.original: The replace function then returns a value that is equal to the following expression: **-** **substr(inpar, 0, index) & repl &** **substr(inpar, index + len, lengthof(inpar) - index - len)**

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: a substr call yields a template with ifpresent
requirements.canonical: If any `substr` call of the `replace` concatenation formula yields a template with the `ifpresent` matching attribute, the attribute SHALL be removed before concatenation and added to the final result of the concatenation.
requirements.original: If any of the substr calls in the previous point would yield a template with the ifpresent matching attribute, this attribute is removed before concatenation and added to the final result of the concatenation.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar refers to a present-restricted template or to a mandatory/unrestricted field
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `replace` contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction, or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the value returned by `replace` SHALL have the present restriction.
requirements.original: If inpar contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record `of, set` `of or array, the` returned value shall have the present restriction.

readings: The returned value SHALL have the present restriction if inpar contains (a) a reference to a template with the present restriction, (b) a matching symbol fulfilling the present restriction, or (c) a reference to an unrestricted template field representing a mandatory record/set field or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array.
The returned value SHALL have the present restriction only if inpar contains a reference to a present-restricted template whose content is such a matching symbol or field reference.
ambiguity.issue: Garbled sentence with unclear scope of "a reference to"; the three-alternative reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar refers to a template with value or omit restriction
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `replace` contains a reference to a template with the value or omit restriction, the value returned by `replace` SHALL have the value restriction.
requirements.original: If inpar contains a reference to a template with the value or omit restriction, the returned value shall have the value restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.canonical: The template returned by the `replace` concatenation formula IS without any length matching attribute, because `substr` removes length matching attributes.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Since the substr function removes length matching attributes, the template returned using the concatenation formula will be without any length matching attribute.

requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.canonical: If inpar or repl of `replace` is not of a string, `record of`, `set of` or array type, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `inpar or repl are not of string, record` `of, set` `of, or array type;`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar and repl have different root types
requirements.canonical: If inpar and repl of `replace` are of different root types, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `inpar and repl are of different root type;`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: index < 0 or index > lengthof(inpar)
requirements.canonical: If the index actual parameter of `replace` is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `index is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar);`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: len < 0 or len > lengthof(inpar)
requirements.canonical: If the len actual parameter of `replace` is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `len is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar);`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-replace
requirements.condition: inpar contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + len > lengthof(inpar)
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `replace` contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index + len is greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: `inpar contains neither AnyValue nor AnyValueOrNone and index+len is greater than` lengthof(inpar).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue
requirements.condition: the actual parameter passed to inpar is a template
requirements.canonical: When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.original:
When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send
statement). The returned bitstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not
make any check on its correctness. The optional encoding_info parameter is used for passing additional encoding
information to the codec and, if it is omitted, no additional information is sent to the codec.

The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value
for this single encvalue call. The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

  - Encoding fails due to a runtime system problem (i.e. no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-o

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-o
requirements.condition: the decoding was successful

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-o
requirements.condition: the decoding was successful

requirements.condition: the decoding was unsuccessful

requirements.original: The return value 0 indicates that decoding was successful.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The return value 1 of `decvalue_o` IS the indication of an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
requirements.original: The return value 1 indicates an unspecified cause of decoding failure.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-o

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-o

requirements.original: The get_stringencoding function analyses the encoded_value and returns the UCS encoding scheme according to clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] (see also clause 27.5 of the present document).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-get-stringencoding

requirements.original: The identified encoding scheme, or the value "<unknown>", if the type of encoding cannot be determined unanimously, shall be returned as a character string.

ambiguity.issue: 'unanimously' is used where 'unambiguously' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:byte-order-mark

ambiguity.issue: 'unanimously' is used where 'unambiguously' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-get-stringencoding

ambiguity.issue: 'unanimously' is used where 'unambiguously' is meant.

requirements.original: remove_bom(in octetstring encoded_value) return octetstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-remove-bom

requirements.original: The remove_bom function removes the optional FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence that may be present at the beginning of a stream of serialized (encoded) universal character strings to indicate the order of the octets within the encoding form, as defined in clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:fn-remove-bom
requirements.condition: encoded_value contains no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence
requirements.canonical: If `encoded_value` contains no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence, `remove_bom` SHALL return the value of `encoded_value` unchanged.
requirements.original: If no FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE sequence present in the encoded_value parameter, the function shall return the value of the parameter without change.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd

requirements.original: The rnd function returns a (pseudo) random number less than 1 but greater or equal to 0.

requirements.subject: ent:random-number-generator

requirements.original: The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd

requirements.original: The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd

requirements.original: If no new seed is provided, the last generated number will be used as seed for the next random number.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:random-number-generator

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd

requirements.original: Thus, the rnd function will always use the seed of the component or control part which calls it.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.
